source.stem:
Multiple choice questions.

System of equations

$$
\left\{ \begin{array}{l} 3 x + 4 y = 5, \\ - 7 x + 9 y = - \frac {5}{2} \end{array} \right.
$$

The solution is ( ).

(A) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 2,\\ y = -0.25 \end{array} \right.$

(B) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -5.5,\\ y = 4 \end{array} \right.$

(C) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = 1,\\ y = 0.5 \end{array} \right.$

(D) $\left\{ \begin{array}{l}x = -1,\\ y = -0.5 \end{array} \right.$

mx.teacher_note: product still holds here even though For 72 = 12 x 6, the prime factors of 12 and 6 combine to form the prime factors of 72 is missing from the stem — on the item about Build the prime factorisation of a product by combining.

mx.name: scope_error
mx.teacher_note: The product rule also covers this: expanding products before factorising when not needed, so it is not an exception — on the item about Build the prime factorisation of a product by combining.

intelligence.enrichment: When a number is first written as a product of two factors, its prime factorisation is obtained by putting together the prime factorisations of those factors.
